name: Navy Green
lede: Navy Green is a dark, strong olive named after the institution rather than a place, and recorded by Maerz and Paul as early as about 1904, decades before the crowd survey that named this exact hex.

sections.title: An institution's word
sections.body:
The library files Navy Green under the place-and-institution tier, built on *navy* the way the plain color [[navy|Navy]] is a manual override for the Royal Navy's dark blue officer's uniform, worn since 1748 [1]. Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary separately records a color word close to this one from about 1904, on plate 22, well before the xkcd 2010 survey that is our only source for the exact hex #35530A [1]. At that hex it measures lightness 32 and chroma 43 in LCH, a dark, strong olive [1].

Its nearest named neighbors are [[army-green|Army Green]], 5.1 CIEDE2000 units off and lighter, and [[deep-green|Deep Green]], 7.3 units off and more vivid [2]. Werner's 1821 nomenclature lists the upper side of yew leaves for a color he called [[duck-green|Duck Green]], 8.3 units away, and the nearest gem comparison is a deep Colombian [[gem:emerald|emerald]], 8.4 units off [2][3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this dark olive in 37 of 23,781 paintings, about 0.16%, as photographed, rarer than 67% of the named colors here [4]. The earliest match is a 1400 painting, about 500 years before Maerz and Paul's circa-1904 record, which only shows an aged, varnished canvas can resemble this hue, not that anyone named it so early, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [4]. It peaks in the 1800s, in 6 of 8,345 paintings, at 1.2 times the archive's overall rate, and inside a painting it most often plays a shadow, in 82% of its matches [4].
